result.question: How did Uzziah trespass against Yahweh?

readings.answer: By entering the LORD’s temple to burn incense on the incense altar.
readings.support: he entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense

readings.answer: By trying to offer incense to the LORD, which he had no right to do.
readings.support: you have no right to offer incense to the LORD

readings.answer: By being in the sanctuary when he should not have been.
readings.support: he entered the temple of the LORD | Leave the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully

assessments.reason: The passage says he entered the LORD’s temple to burn incense on the altar of incense, which matches burning incense in Yahweh’s house.
Offering incense is the act of burning incense, and “trying to offer incense” aligns with “he entered… to burn incense,” which the priests say he had no right to do.

The text targets the act of offering/burning incense as the trespass (“you have no right to offer incense… only the priests… are consecrated to burn incense”; “he entered… to burn incense”); mere presence in the sanctuary is not identified as the offense.

result.reason: The window clearly states Uzziah’s trespass was attempting to burn/offer incense in the LORD’s temple, a duty reserved for priests.
